title: United Provinces of Central America
capsule: The Federal Republic of Central America (formally Provinces United of Central America) was established in 1823 when the former Captaincy General of Guatemala declared independence from the Mexican Empire of Agustín de Iturbide, comprising the five provinces of Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Nicaragua, and Costa Rica. The federation was plagued from its inception by conflict between Liberal and Conservative factions, between the capital Guatemala City and provincial interests, and by the costly guerrilla war against Rafael Carrera's Conservative rebellion; Liberal president Francisco Morazán attempted to hold the union together through military force but failed. The republic dissolved in 1839–1840 as individual states declared independence; Morazán was executed in 1842, ending any realistic hope of reunification.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The federation's outer boundaries correspond to the former colonial captaincy-general and are well-defined; internal provincial demarcations were disputed throughout the republic's existence.
